title: Customer-network rolling evidence compact protocol
body:
OBJECTIVE:
Provide a compact, rolling evidence protocol for customer-managed networking changes that satisfies audit needs while minimizing telemetry surface area and bandwidth for low-bandwidth or high-sensitivity customers. This is intended as a lightweight alternative to full immutable evidence bundles — intended to be sufficient for gating, quick investigations, and rollback decisions.

CONTEXT / PROBLEM STATEMENT:
- Customers using Private mode require tamper-evident records of VPC changes, peering updates, and operator-approved configuration deltas.
- Full forensic bundles (snapshots, pcap, full config history) are heavy and often impractical for customers with constrained egress or strict data retention policies.
- Product team needs a consistent API/UX for approval gates that relies on a minimal set of cryptographic attestations and compact change proofs.

GOALS:
- Define a compact evidence payload that can be produced by Redwood operator UI or by a customer-side agent.
- Ensure proofs support: approval rationale, operator identity, time bounds, and an integrity checksum of the change-set.
- Support streaming/rolling evidence (incremental) so long-term retention is small but reconstructable when needed.
- Provide clear mapping to approval gate states and rollback triggers in the control plane.

NON-GOALS:
- This doc does not replace full forensic snapshot workflows for high-risk incidents.
- Not a replacement for SIEM exports or customers' own packet capture retention.

TERMS / DEFINITIONS (informal):
- compact-evidence: minimal JSON payload containing metadata + cryptographic digest + incremental delta index.
- epoch-hash: a sequence-hash that chains increments (rolling) to provide tamper evidence without full payloads.
- attestation-token: operator-signed token (RS256) that asserts approval decision + minimal context.

USER STORIES:
- As a Customer Network Owner, I want to see a short, cryptographically-linked summary of each VPC change so I can sign off without downloading large bundles.
- As an SRE on Redwood, I want to be able to request a compact-evidence stream for a tenant and verify integrity locally for triage.
- As a Compliance Reviewer, I want an export that shows approval decisions + chained epoch-hashes for a date range.

COMPACT EVIDENCE PAYLOAD (proposed fields):
- version: protocol version string (e.g. "v1")
- tenant_id: obfuscated tenant id (internal UUID)
- change_id: short id for this delta (base62, 12 chars)
- parent_epoch: previous epoch-hash or null
- epoch_hash: sha256(base64) of the compact payload and parent_epoch (chaining)
- summary: free-text one-line description (operator input or automated diff)
- delta_digest: sha256 of the serialized minimal-delta (not included inline unless requested)
- attestations: list of short attestations (see below)
- retention_class: short enum: [ephemeral, standard, longterm]
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- preview: small human-friendly snippet of the change (<= 512 bytes)
- proof_refs: optional short refs to stored artifacts (s3:// or internal ids)

ATTESTATION OBJECT (compact):
- actor: name or service (e.g. "operator:l.chen")
- role: operator | customer-admin | system
- verdict: approve | reject | veto | auto-approve
- reason_code: short code (ACCEPT_RISK, SECURITY_FLAG, AUTO_ROLLBACK_TRIGGER)
- signature: RS256 compact JWS over (tenant_id|change_id|epoch_hash|timestamp)

BEHAVIORAL PATTERNS:
- Rolling mode (default): Generate compact-evidence for every commit/change. Each payload references previous epoch_hash creating a lightweight chain. The chain enables reconstructing the ordered changes without full diffs.
- Snapshot-on-demand: If a reviewer requests full evidence, we assemble full snapshot bundle and attach as proof_ref; this operation is logged and rate-limited.
- Day-bound export: A daily digest that includes the day's final epoch_hash and a short index of change_ids; used for compliance exports.

APPROVAL GATE STATES MAPPING (control-plane consequences):
- PENDING: compact-evidence created, no attestation yet; UI shows "waiting" and an auto-reminder is queued.
- UNDER_REVIEW: attestation(s) present but not majority/required roles; limited rollout suppressed.
- APPROVED: required attestations present; control plane may apply change or queue for scheduled apply.
- VETOED: at least one veto attestation present; triggers a rollback or prevents apply.
- EXPIRED: no action within X hours; gateway optionally auto-rollback depending on policy.

OPERATOR RUNBOOK (quick):
- How to generate compact-evidence from the UI: operator enters short summary -> system creates delta_digest -> epoch_hash computed -> operator signs attestation via UI.
- How to verify locally: use redwoodctl verify-evidence --payload <json> which checks signatures and re-computes epoch chain.
- Requesting full bundle: redwoodctl request-bundle --change <change_id> creates a ticket (JIRA link) and kicks off bundle assembly into a temporary store (proof_refs returned).

TELEMETRY / SAMPLING & PRIVACY:
- Default retention_class for customer-managed networks is "standard" (30 days). Customers can request "ephemeral" (7 days) or "longterm" (365 days) per contract.
- For customers in low-bandwidth regions, rolling evidence defaults to "preview-only" where delta_digest is recorded but full-deltas are never uploaded unless snapshot-on-demand is triggered by the customer.
- Telemetry events to emit (small): evidence_created, attestation_signed, bundle_requested, bundle_ready, evidence_exported. Each event is O(100) bytes.

SECURITY & CRYPTOGRAPHIC NOTES:
- Signatures use customer-managed KMS where available (HSM-backed). When KMS is not available, Redwood operator keys are used but stored in HSM and audited.
- epoch_hash chaining uses SHA-256. Consider migrating to an extendable hash (e.g. BLAKE2) if performance matters for very high change rates.
- Attestations must include sequence-nonce to avoid replay.

API SURFACE (sketch):
- POST /v1/private/tenants/{tenant}/evidence (body=compact-evidence) -> 201 change_id
- GET  /v1/private/tenants/{tenant}/evidence/{change_id} -> compact-evidence payload or 404
- GET  /v1/private/tenants/{tenant}/evidence?from={date}&to={date}&type=rolling -> paginated list of compact-evidence summaries
- POST /v1/private/tenants/{tenant}/evidence/{change_id}/bundle-request -> enqueue bundle assembly, returns proof_ref

DATA MODELS / STORAGE NOTES:
- Store compact-evidence as small JSON with TTL based on retention_class. epoch_hash chain stored as index to speed verification.
- Full bundles archived to cold storage (opt-in) and only accessible via authenticated proof_ref.

OPERATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS / COST:
- Rolling evidence cut costs dramatically compared to always storing snapshots. Estimate: 0.5KB-1.5KB per event vs 20-200KB per full snapshot.
- Bandwidth implications: for customers with extreme egress limits, use preview-only mode and on-demand bundles.
- Rate limits: bundle requests limited per tenant per day (configurable by contract).

MIGRATION STRATEGY / ROLLOUT PHASES:
- Phase 0 (experiment): opt-in for 10 pilot customers; collect signals (bundle request frequency, verification failures).
- Phase 1 (beta): enable on new tenants with default rolling evidence; add UI indicators for chain health.
- Phase 2 (shipped): provide tenant-level retention controls and KMS key binding for attestations.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- What is the canonical attestation key rotation cadence for customer-managed keys? (30d, 90d?)
- Exact expiry policy for pending approvals that never get attested (PENDING -> EXPIRED threshold).
- Are epoch_hash chains stored client-side for higher assurance, or only server-side with export endpoints?

IMPLEMENTATION TODOs (short-term):
- Prototype redwoodctl verify-evidence + epoch-chain checker (eng-applied-ml + infra).
- UI: add "compact evidence" flow to operator change submission (console team).
- Policy: default retention classes and contract language for longterm retention (legal/product).

REFERENCES / LINKS:
- Confluence: PD Private Onboarding (PD-ONBOARD-432)
- Related Jira: PD-1287 (evidence prototyping)
- Internal RFC: private-evidence-2025 (draft)

NOTES TO REVIEWERS:
- This is a draft intended to capture a minimally viable compact evidence protocol for customer-managed networking changes. Looking for feedback on the attestation token shape and recommended retention defaults.

REVISION HISTORY:
- 2025-09-18 - initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-11-03 - added preview-only mode and sampling notes (Liam)
- 2026-02-20 - cryptographic recommendations and API sketch added (Rina)
